malodorous

mal-OH-dur-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Malodorous is having a very unpleasant smell.

No one wanted to sit near the malodorous dumpster behind the restaurant on the hottest afternoons of summer.

Example

A malodorous cloud drifted from the paper mill whenever the wind shifted toward town.

A cloud drifting from a paper mill that everyone notices and dislikes is exactly malodorous.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

foul-smelling: Foul-smelling is the plain, everyday way of saying something gives off an offensive odor. Malodorous means the same thing in a more formal, bookish register -- the word a report or a novel reaches for where ordinary speech would say foul-smelling.

noxious: Noxious means actually harmful -- fumes or gases that can injure whoever breathes them, not merely offend the nose. Malodorous is about offense rather than danger: a malodorous smell is seriously unpleasant but may be perfectly harmless.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

fragrant: having a pleasant, sweet smell

Where it sits · how foul the odor is — smelly → malodorous → putrid

smelly vs. malodorous: Smelly is the casual, everyday word for something that smells bad -- gym socks, an old sponge; malodorous is a stronger, more formal word for a smell that is seriously, insistently unpleasant.

putrid vs. malodorous: Putrid pushes the smell to the point of active decay or rot, while malodorous simply means unpleasant, without necessarily implying decomposition.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — mal-

prefix — mal-: bad (Latin)

root — odor

root — odor: smell (Latin)

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Malodorous combines mal- ('bad') + odor ('smell') + -ous -- literally 'possessing a bad smell.'

Use the root in a new word: deodorant

Use the root in a new word: deodorant: The same odor root, with the opposite prefix de- ('away from'), gives us the everyday word deodorant -- something designed to take a bad smell away.
